 Valencia v Villarreal: Javier Aguirre targets first win to welcome Pitchwise Holdings 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Valencia face Villarreal at Mestalla in a derby framed by urgent need and a shifting boardroom. Javier Aguirre is still waiting for his first win after two draws, and three points would ease pressure on a penultimate-placed side.
 According to Superdeporte, Pitchwise Holdings’ entry involves a planned 42 percent stake and a 100 million euro capital injection, with Meriton Holdings remaining the majority shareholder. It is unclear how much could be directed to signings by Braulio Vázquez in January, with greater spend expected in summer.
 OneFootball Videos
 On the pitch, Valencia remain in trouble. They sit penultimate in LaLiga, and Mañas prevented Málaga beating Alavés, a result that would have left them bottom. The derby now carries added weight.
 Aguirre has opened with draws against Racing de Santander and Athletic Club. Performances have improved with adjustments, but the side still need goals, defensive solidity and, above all, points to get out of danger.
 Mestalla is expected to be central to any turnaround. Aguirre appealed to his players’ character and the crowd’s backing, saying the group need a win and continuity in their play, that morale is good but a victory could free them.
 The coach will still be without Umar Sadiq, Copete and Dimitri Foulquier as they recover. He wants more intensity, pressing and cutting edge to exploit Iñigo Pérez’s Villarreal, who lost at Anfield in the Champions League, drew with Elche, and sit 12th on nine points.
 A home win would deliver a timely lift and a fitting welcome for Pitchwise Holdings.
 Source: Superdeporte
